title: role-templates-service-account-creation-flow-notes
body:
Purpose and scope:
- Capture quick UX thinking for: role templates (predefined RBAC roles), service account key creation flow, and inline audit-log context in the org/team settings console.
- Focus on flow clarity for platform admins and SREs who will provision service accounts for CI pipelines or private deployments.
- This doc is intentionally lightweight; use as input for next UX spike and grooming.

Summary of proposed flow (3 main screens):
1) Role Templates Library (list/grid)
   - Top-level area under Org Settings > Roles & Service Accounts.
   - Default templates: Owner, Admin, Reader, Inference-Invoker, Embeddings-Indexer, Billing-Viewer.
   - Each tile/row: template name, short description, principal permission summary (3 bullets), last updated, an "Apply to team" CTA, and three-dot menu (edit, duplicate, delete, export-json).
   - Quick search + filter by permission (e.g., "read-costs", "invoke-models", "manage-keys").
   - Wireframe notes: compact card with expandable permission list on hover — mobile first collapse.

2) Create Service Account (multi-step modal / page)
   - Step 1: Basics
     - Fields: Name (required), Description (optional), Assign to Org/Team dropdown (autocomplete), Expiration (optional, ISO date picker), Tags.
     - Microcopy: "Service accounts are machine identities used by CI, workers, and infra. Keys are shown once."
   - Step 2: Role assignment
     - UI: type-ahead to pick one or multiple role templates OR create inline custom role (permission matrix minimal UI).
     - If template chosen, show a diff view if team inherited policies tighten (e.g., "template grants invoke-models; team policy blocks network access").
     - Suggestion: default to least-privilege template suggested by use-case selection dropdown (CI/CD, batch inference, metrics exporter).
   - Step 3: Key options and delivery
     - Single-use vs long-lived key toggle. Recommend short-lived by default (7d) with rotation reminders.
     - Key material delivery options: download JSON (shown once), send to KMS envelope (if configured), copy to clipboard (with ephemeral confirmation), or push to Secrets Manager integration (AWS/GCP/Azure) via configured connector.
     - Warn: "This key will be shown only once. Save it now or configure Secrets integration."
     - Audit hint: show a live preview of audit log entry that will be generated on create (small panel on right).
   - Step 4: Review & create
     - Show compact summary: name, assigned team, effective permissions (flattened), key expiry, delivery method.
     - CTA: "Create service account and generate key" and secondary "Create without key (use external identity)".

3) Service Account Details + Audit context
   - Tabs: Overview, Keys (history), Roles & Grants, Activity (audit log slice), Integrations.
   - Keys tab: list of generated keys, created_by, created_at, expiration, method (download/KMS/push), last_seen IP (if available), rotate/delete actions. For each key, a small audit summary line: who created it, from which IP, and which client (UI/API).
   - Activity tab: pre-filtered audit-log view for the selected service account. Provide inline search and filters (action type, actor, time range).
   - Inline contextual help: links to docs about best practices (rotate, restrict scopes, rotate-backed secrets).

Edge cases and guardrails:
- If user tries to create a service account with admin-level role templates in a non-admin team, show a policy violation modal explaining why and offering "request exception" path (creates ticket for org admin).
- Disallow export of keys if org settings forbid external key material download; instead enforce KMS-only.
- When assigning multiple roles, compute and show an aggregated permission set and highlight conflicts (allow vs deny).
- Provide an "emergency revoke" action on SA details that rotates all keys and optionally creates a sync task to update integrated secrets managers.

Accessibility and keyboard interactions:
- Modal must trap focus; stepper accessible via keyboard; keyboard shortcut to open "Create service account" (g then s?).
- Ensure copy to clipboard provides accessible confirmation (aria-live region) and has time-limited fallback (show masked key for 30s).

Telemetry & success metrics (grooming for product):
- Conversion: clicks on Create -> completed SA + key generated rate.
- Time to create SA (median).
- % of keys delivered via Secrets Manager vs download. Goal to increase Secrets Manager usage to 80% within Q2 for enterprise accounts.
- Number of policy exceptions requested and time to resolve.
- Audit coverage: percent of SA actions that have correlating audit entries with IP/client.

Backlog/implementation notes (prioritized):
- MUST: Role Templates Library UI + CRUD (RED-2413).
- MUST: Service account create flow skeleton (modal with steps) (RED-2440).
- SHOULD: Key delivery integrations (Secrets Manager, KMS) (RED-2501).
- SHOULD: Audit-log baked preview while creating key (small panel) (RED-2468).
- MAY: Inline policy conflict resolution suggestions using policy engine (later).
- Nice-to-have: Default role suggestions based on project name or detected CI provider (heuristics).

Acceptance criteria (for initial MVP sprint):
- Admin can create/edit/delete role templates.
- Admin can create a service account bound to a team and choose one role template.
- System generates a key (download only) and shows key once; key entry recorded in audit log.
- Service account details page shows keys tab and activity tab with audit entries.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How granular should out-of-the-box role templates be? Too many templates = confusion; too few = lots of custom roles. Proposal: ship 6 common templates, add API for orgs to create more.
- Do we allow cross-team SA assignment by default? Potential security risk. Default: restrict to same org then explicit checkbox to allow cross-team usage with justification.
- Rotation UX: should we offer automated rotation schedules per key? Implementation complexity vs value.
- Should audit preview include raw JSON that will be written? (risk: leak). Maybe masked by default.

Copy / microcopy suggestions (short lines we can iterate in Figma):
- Create SA header: "Create service account" with small hint: "Machine identity for jobs, CI, and infra. Keys shown once."
- Key delivery hint: "Recommended: push to your Secrets Manager. Only choose download for debugging/testing."
- Policy violation modal: "This action is blocked by org policy. Request exception or choose a different role."

Next steps / immediate tasks for UX spike:
- Aisha: make 3 quick Figma frames (list, create modal step 2 role selector, detail page keys) — due 2026-03-17.
- Mark: spike backend requirements for secrets connector (OAuth flow, service account in cloud providers) — due 2026-03-19.
- Ravi: prototype audit-preview small component in console (mock data) — due 2026-03-20.
- Schedule 30m sync with security and SRE to review default templates and policy enforcement model (invite list: org-security, eng-sre leads).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc. Expect many short-hand lines and TODOs. Add comments inline (Figma or Linear) for UI trade-offs.
- Prioritize least-privilege defaults and integration with org-wide KMS/secrets managers for enterprise customers.

Historical context / references:
- See older notes in shared_drives/product/security-and-compliance/service-account-guidelines-2025.json (for past policy decisions).
- Related: access-management-audit-log-and-keys-ux-notes.json — do not duplicate; this doc is focused on role template + SA creation flow.

Revision log:
- 2026-02-15: initial draft (Lena).
- 2026-02-20: added audit-preview idea (Ravi).
- 2026-03-10: prioritized backlog & added acceptance criteria (Aisha).

Quick UX sketches: (paste small ascii if helpful)
[Role templates list]  [Create SA CTA]  [Search]
[Card] Role: Inference-Invoker
 - Perms: invoke-models, read-model-metadata, use-kv-cache
 - Apply to team -> dropdown

End of doc.
